title: Declare the case set as data and refuse to run on a bad one
problem: The harness needs a set of cases to run. If cases live in code, adding one is a code change and the case set stops being something a non-author can extend. If a malformed case set is tolerated, every later comparison silently compares different populations.
context: This is the first task of a learner-authored forge project. No source exists yet. The learner creates the repository, chooses its structure, and owns every design decision inside the specification's constraints.
impact: The case set is the population every later measurement is taken over. If it can drift silently, nothing built on top of it means anything.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cases are declared in a data file. A case can be added, edited or removed with no source change.
Every case has a stable identifier that survives reordering and editing of other cases.
A malformed case set is refused before any case runs. The error names the offending case and what is wrong with it.
A refused case set produces no run record and no partial output.
Automated tests cover at least one valid case set and at least two distinct malformed ones, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains the chosen case identity scheme, one rejected alternative, and what breaks first if two cases are given the same identifier.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only. No configuration framework, schema library or CLI framework for this task.
Do not implement running, recording or comparison yet. This task ends at a validated, loaded case set.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: One input boundary and its validation.

investigation_areas: What identifies a case, and what must stay stable when the file is edited
Which malformations are worth detecting and which are not worth the code
How the loader reports a problem so the reader can fix it without reading the loader
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design; the learner chooses the runner and the layout.
documentation_requirements: Record the case file format, the identity scheme and the rejected alternative in the learner design.

next_task_preview.title: Run the case set against a target and record the run immutably
next_task_preview.summary: Execute each case, keep going when one raises, and write a run record that a later run can never overwrite.
